html:
The system by which the richest citizens of Athens paid directly for public needs. Each such duty was called a liturgy, a word meaning work for the people.

The two best known were:

  • the trierarchy: a rich man paid to fit out and run a trireme, a warship, for a year, and often commanded it himself
  • the choregia: a rich man paid for the chorus of a play or song at a festival, its training and costumes

Rich men competed to spend lavishly, since it won them honour and votes. The young Pericles paid for the chorus of The Persians by Aeschylus in 472 BCE. A man who thought another was richer could challenge him to take on the duty or swap their whole property.

Athens had no regular tax on wealth or income, so liturgies did that job through honour and pressure. They paid for much of the navy that held the Delian League and the theatre of the golden age.
sum: The system by which the richest citizens of Athens paid directly for public needs. Each such duty was called a liturgy, a word meaning work for the people.
